result.citation: San Diego Mun. Code § 98.1101 et seq. (Ord. O-21955 N.S.)
result.official_quote: (a) It is unlawful for a person to sell, license, or otherwise provide an algorithmic device to a landlord. (b) It is unlawful for a landlord to use an algorithmic device to set rental rates or occupancy levels for residential rental property. (a) A tenant may seek injunctive relief, damages, or civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation of this Division, in a civil action against a landlord.
result.note: Cites the whole adopted Division 11 as § 98.1101 et seq. (Ord. O-21955 N.S.) because the card merges the ban in § 98.1103 with the definition in § 98.1102 and the remedies in § 98.1104. The quote now comes from the adopted code text in D074, not the draft in D076. The card should also be checked against D074 on two points: attorney's fees go to a prevailing landlord or tenant, and the adopted definition is limited to nonpublic competitor data of two or more landlords.
